tonight.headline: Chicago may start a quarterback who last played in 2023, and your tight end catches his passes
body: Week 3 has not started and nothing is locked. Matthew Golden kicks off first, tomorrow at 18:15 Mexico City, and he is correctly in your flex.

The live thing is Colston Loveland. Caleb Williams did not practise Wednesday with a hamstring, Tyson Bagent is in concussion protocol and not at the facility, and Ben Johnson said 'Case is the one that's practising today.' Case Keenum has not played since 2023. Loveland faces the defence allowing the fewest fantasy points to tight ends. You have until Monday 18:15 to decide, but the add that gives you the option costs nothing and should happen now.

case.label: Why this is the headline
case.body: This is the exact failure this system was built around. A tight end projected 9.8 scored 0.0 because his team were down to a third-string quarterback, it was reported everywhere two days early, and the brief had a startable alternative on the bench. Loveland projects 9.7. The shape is identical.

case.label: What the file cannot tell you
case.body: Nothing in the league file names a quarterback. Loveland's 9.7 is an ESPN projection that does not know Chicago's depth chart has collapsed two deep this week.

case.label: The other side
case.body: Williams has not been ruled out. Johnson called the hamstring low-grade and said Williams was actively involved in a walkthrough. Chicago play Monday, which is the maximum possible recovery runway. The base case is genuinely still that Williams plays.

case.label: Falsified if
case.body: Chicago list Williams as a full participant on Friday or Saturday. The swap then never fires, the tight end seat is untouched, and the only cost was a roster spot that was occupied by a backup quarterback who cannot score in this league.

doFirst.deadlineLabel: Los Angeles kick off Sunday 11:00 Mexico City
doFirst.title: Add Oronde Gadsden II, drop Matthew Stafford
doFirst.subtitle: Gadsden is a free agent, so this costs zero never-resetting priority. Stafford is a backup quarterback in a one-quarterback league — he cannot score for you in any week this season.

case.label: The drop
case.body: Matthew Stafford has been on your bench behind Trevor Lawrence all season. IPADE starts one quarterback and the flex is slot 23, which takes RB, WR and TE — never a quarterback. There is no lineup in which Stafford's 14.8 becomes a point for you.

case.label: The add
case.body: Sports Illustrated name Gadsden a Week 3 streamer at 7% rostered nationally. He scored in Week 1, and both David Njoku and Charlie Koler are on injured reserve, so the tight end room ahead of him is empty rather than crowded. He draws Buffalo.

case.label: Why a tight end and not a receiver
case.body: Your standing strategy note says the IPADE flex taking a tight end means a second startable tight end has real value here and none in Chem. This is the week that stops being theoretical: the tight end you already own may be catching passes from a third-string quarterback on Monday night.

case.label: The honest weakness
case.body: ESPN projects Gadsden 8.7 against Loveland's 9.7, so on the numbers alone this is a downgrade, and the strategy floor says a move that lowers projected points needs a stated reason. The stated reason is that Loveland's 9.7 assumes a quarterback Chicago may not have. Adding Gadsden does not commit you to starting him — it buys the option for the price of a player who has no use.

case.label: Falsified if
case.body: Buffalo hold Gadsden under four targets while Njoku or Koler are activated, which would say the vacancy that created his role is closing. Or Chicago clear Caleb Williams to full participation, in which case the add was cheap insurance that went unused rather than a mistake.

action.label: Add Oronde Gadsden II · drop Matthew Stafford

doFirst.deadlineLabel: Fallback only — arm it on Saturday, not today
doFirst.title: If Chicago name Keenum, start Gadsden at tight end over Loveland
doFirst.subtitle: Unarmed. Fires only if Caleb Williams is ruled out or listed doubtful, or Chicago name Case Keenum the starter.

case.label: Who is throwing
case.body: Ben Johnson, Wednesday: 'We're at a point right now, not sure who the starter's going to be on Monday night. Case is the one that's practising today.' Williams did not practise with a low-grade hamstring and is week-to-week. Bagent is in concussion protocol and not at the facility. CBS Sports report Keenum has not played since 2023, when he started two games for Houston.

case.label: The matchup on top of it
case.body: Sports Illustrated named Loveland their sit of the week: outside the top seventy tight ends through two games, against the Eagles defence allowing the fewest fantasy points to the position. That is a bad draw before the quarterback question, and a Keenum start makes it a bad draw behind a quarterback who has not taken a meaningful snap in three years.

case.label: Why this is a branch and not a decision
case.body: The tight end seat changed hands this morning — T.J. Hockenson was dropped — and the standing churn rule closes a seat for seven days unless someone in it is ruled out. Williams is not ruled out. So this card waits for the condition rather than pre-empting it, and the churn rule is respected rather than argued with.

case.label: What would change it
case.body: Chicago listing Williams as a full participant on Friday or Saturday, which closes the card at no cost. Or Philadelphia's tight end numbers being an artifact of facing two teams with no tight end — which is checkable and which I could not check this run, because no defence-versus-position table would render.

doFirst.deadlineLabel: Fallback only — check Thursday morning after waivers clear
doFirst.title: If Carnell Tate clears waivers unclaimed, add him for Jonah Coleman
doFirst.subtitle: Unarmed, and deliberately not a claim. Waivers clear at 01:00 Mexico City tonight. If nobody takes him he becomes a free agent and costs you nothing.

case.label: Why he is worth the seat
case.body: FantasyPros have Tate holding a 23.8% adjusted target share across consecutive weeks — a target-share leader, not a one-week spike. Sports Illustrated list him among their Week 3 must-start receivers. He is rostered in 86.5% of leagues nationally and sits on this wire.

case.label: Why this is not a claim
case.body: IPADE priority never resets and you sit sixth. Your standing rule spends it only on a player who starts immediately or wins a league. Tate projects 11.8 against Matthew Golden's 11.4 in your flex — a four-tenths upgrade. Spending a season-long chip on four tenths of a point is precisely the trade the rule exists to prevent.

case.label: The drop
case.body: Jonah Coleman, who carries a sprained ankle and a 1.7 projection and is the same player the Chem brief is dropping today. He was claimed with this league's priority yesterday, which is a separate mistake already recorded, and holding him does not unspend it.

case.label: The collision worth knowing
case.body: Tate plays for Tennessee and you start the Giants D/ST against Tennessee on Sunday. Adding him means one of your two starters is rooting against the other. It is a real cost and it is smaller than the gap between a target-share leader and a hurt fourth running back.

case.label: What would change it
case.body: Another manager claiming him overnight, which ends the branch and costs nothing. Or Tennessee naming a different quarterback, which changes the target share the whole case rests on.

whatWentWrong.title: The tight end seat was emptied this morning and the quarterback question arrived this afternoon
whatWentWrong.lead: T.J. Hockenson was dropped early this morning and the seat was closed on churn grounds until 30 September. Six hours later Chicago's quarterback room collapsed to a third-stringer.

case.label: The sequence
case.body: Hockenson dropped this morning, Loveland held on a churn argument whose stated premise was that Tyson Bagent would be throwing to him. Bagent has been in concussion protocol since the Week 2 loss to Minnesota — the reporting predates this morning's brief.

case.label: Why it connects to the cards above
case.body: It is the reason the first card exists and the reason the second is a branch rather than a decision. The seat is closed to churn; it is not closed to adding depth against a named risk while dropping a player who cannot score.

case.label: The fair reading
case.body: The churn rule was applied correctly on the information the morning run used. What it did not do was check who was throwing — which is the one check this runbook puts above all the others.

case.label: Falsified if
case.body: Bagent clears protocol by Friday and is named the starter. The premise is then restored, the hold was right, and only the reasoning was lucky.

whatWentWrong.sources: CBS Sports · Sports Illustrated · Bleacher Nation

whatWentWrong.title: Never-resetting priority is gone, spent on a running back projecting 1.7
whatWentWrong.lead: Jonah Coleman was claimed with this league's priority. He is the drop on the third card today, which is what that decision looks like twenty-four hours later.

case.label: What was spent
case.body: IPADE waiver priority never resets. One claim drops you to last for the rest of the season. It went on a Denver running back who carries a sprained ankle and a 1.7 projection.

case.label: Why it matters this week specifically
case.body: Carnell Tate is sitting on waivers tonight at 86.5% national ownership. Priority would have been the clean way to take him. It is not available, which is exactly why the third card waits for him to clear into free agency instead — the only route left.

case.label: The part that is not a disaster
case.body: Tate is a four-tenths upgrade on your current flex, so even with priority in hand the rule would have said no. The cost of the Coleman claim is not this week's receiver; it is the league-winner in week eight that you now cannot claim.

case.label: What would change it
case.body: Denver ruling Dobbins and Harvey out while clearing Coleman, which would make him a starting running back and the claim defensible in hindsight. Friday's report settles it.

whatWentWrong.sources: ESPN league file · activity log · Bleacher Report

whatWentWrong.title: Rashee Rice has now had three quiet weeks and he is still starting
whatWentWrong.lead: Four catches on six targets for 83 yards in the Week 2 overtime win. NBC's headline word was 'modest'. He starts anyway, and the reason is that nothing beats him without spending something you do not have.

case.label: The usage
case.body: Six targets in a game that went to overtime is a small share of a large pie. The standing read since 22 September has treated him as a sell-high candidate rather than a fixture, and Week 2 did not contradict it.

case.label: The alternative on your own bench
case.body: Devaughn Vele is a Sports Illustrated must-start this week and projects 11.6 against Rice's 12.8. The optimiser actually prefers Vele in the flex over Matthew Golden by two-tenths. That is inside the noise, and Golden's case — 18 targets tied for the team lead, a team-high 69 routes run, WR22 for the week — is made of reporting where Vele's is made of a ranking.

case.label: Why this connects to the cards
case.body: It is the reason no receiver card exists. The third card spends the one free seat on Tate only if he clears, because a receiver upgrade inside a point is not worth a claim and not worth a churn.

case.label: Falsified if
case.body: Rice posts a 20%-plus target share at Miami. That closes the sell-high read and he goes back to being a fixture. A third week under 15% makes him a sell at whatever the name still pays.

trades.theirGainLine: Their gain is +1.6 a week — Tuten steps straight into their RB2 slot ahead of Rachaad White's 9.4, and Lamar Jackson is currently worth exactly zero to them because Josh Allen starts every week.

case.label: Re-verified against tonight's snapshot
case.body: Lamar Jackson still sits at slot 20 on Team 13, behind Josh Allen at slot 0, in a one-quarterback league. Rachaad White is still their slot-2 starter at 9.4, which is the weakness Tuten fixes. Their only injury flag is DJ Moore. Nothing that would pull this offer has happened since it was written on 19 September.

case.label: The slot check
case.body: Run before the offer, because a run once asked a team for its starting quarterback and shipped it twice. Allen is slot 0 and starting; Lamar is slot 20 and benched. You are asking for the one they are not using.

case.label: The arithmetic, both sides
case.body: Your optimal lineup goes 119.9 to 123.6, so +3.7, entirely at quarterback: Lawrence 16.4 out, Lamar 20.1 in. Theirs goes 123.6 to 125.2, so +1.6, entirely at running back: White 9.4 out, Tuten 11.0 in. Both numbers come from tonight's snapshot, recomputed, not carried.

case.label: The honest risk
case.body: This is priced on one week. Over a season Tuten is a young back with standalone value and Lamar is a top-two quarterback, which is a bigger gap in your favour than 3.7 a week suggests — but it is also why they may say no. Odds are LONGSHOT because the offer is correctly lopsided in your favour on season value and the other manager can see that.

case.label: Do not re-send
case.body: This is a standing row, not an instruction. It was sent on 19 September. Respond if they open the conversation or counter; do not push it again, which reads as desperation and lowers the price.

case.label: Falsified if
case.body: Team 13 acquire or start a second real running back, which kills their gain. Or they trade or drop a quarterback, which kills the surplus. Or Lamar Jackson appears on a Baltimore injury report — he is not on this week's, checked tonight. Or Saquon Barkley is ruled out for Week 3, which makes Tuten your starter and the offer must be pulled before it is accepted.

trades.sources: ESPN league file · recomputed from the 21:52Z snapshot
trades.copyText: Hey — you're carrying Josh Allen and Lamar Jackson in a one-QB league, so one of them scores you nothing every week. I'll give you Bhayshul Tuten for Lamar. Straight up. By my math it's worth about +1.6 a week to you right now because Tuten walks into your RB2 spot over Rachaad White, and Lamar is worth zero to you as long as Allen starts. I'm not pretending it doesn't help me — it does, I need a QB. But it's the rare one that actually helps us both. Yes or no, no hard feelings either way.

worthALook.name: Adonai Mitchell
worthALook.lead: The receiver taking the targets away from your own starter, and a free agent here.

case.label: The role
case.body: FantasyPros: a team-high twelve targets for 63 yards in Week 2 and a 31.0% adjusted target share, which they describe as massive growth. His ownership moved +11.90 in a day from a low base — the MONEY-band shape, rising fast because the market has seen the snap counts.

case.label: Why it matters to you twice
case.body: Garrett Wilson starts for you in both leagues and drew seven targets in that same game. Mitchell is either the reason Wilson is capped or the hedge against it. Owning both sides of a target share you cannot predict is a legitimate answer in a ten-team league.

case.label: Why he is not a card
case.body: He costs a roster seat and all three of your seats this week are committed — Gadsden takes Stafford's, Tate takes Coleman's if he clears. A fourth move would be churn wearing a suit.

case.label: When to act
case.body: If Tate is claimed overnight, Mitchell is the better use of Coleman's seat than nothing — he is a free agent so there is no claim to lose. If Wilson clears nine targets at Detroit, this row closes and the Jets read was wrong.

worthALook.name: Saints D/ST
worthALook.lead: The defence comparison, answered hold — and this is the unit that nearly changed the answer.

case.label: The case for them
case.body: FanDuel name New Orleans one of three Week 3 streams: home against a Las Vegas offence with an immobile quarterback short on passing-game weapons, and the Saints favoured despite Vegas being 2-0. They sit at DST9 in the league file's own rank and 4.1% owned.

case.label: Why the Giants keep the seat
case.body: FanDuel rate the Giants' draw a smash spot on the same board — Cameron Ward sacked five times already after 55 as a rookie in 2025. FantasyPros rank the Giants DST10; they do not rank New Orleans at all, and the DST9 I am comparing against is the league file's own rank, which is a weaker unit of comparison and is stated as such. One rank on mismatched scales is not a reason to spend a roster move, and your standing rule is that a stream gaining 0.3 points costs a move for nothing.

case.label: The thing that would flip it
case.body: Giants pass rushers on Friday's report, or Tennessee naming a quarterback other than Ward. Either makes the matchup rather than the unit the thing that was right.

case.label: What would change it
case.body: The Giants finishing outside the top fifteen defences in Week 3 while New Orleans finish top five. The seat then reopens on 30 September when the churn window expires, and it is a free-agent move either way — never a claim, in this league, for a defence.

doNotChase.name: Tank Bigsby
doNotChase.lead: Yesterday's fallback card, closed today. The condition did not fire and there is no longer a seat to fire it into.

case.label: Why it was armed
case.body: He is Saquon Barkley's direct backup and a free agent here, so a handcuff at zero priority cost. The card was published unarmed, to be triggered only if Barkley were ruled out or doubtful.

case.label: Why it closes
case.body: Rapoport's reporting has the MRI as 'more cautious than anything else' with the hope of a minor injury, and Barkley played through the stinger. He has not been ruled out, he has not been listed doubtful, and Philadelphia play Monday. The base case, stated honestly in yesterday's own card, was that this never arms.

case.label: The seat problem
case.body: Yesterday the paired drop was Matthew Stafford. Stafford is being spent today on Oronde Gadsden, and Jonah Coleman is spoken for by the Tate branch. There is no third seat, and inventing one by dropping MarShawn Lloyd would repeat a mistake this log already records.

case.label: What would change it
case.body: Philadelphia ruling Barkley out or listing him doubtful on Saturday. At that point Bigsby matters more than either pending card and the drop becomes Coleman. Note the second risk: if Philadelphia name Will Shipley rather than Bigsby as the lead replacement, this is the wrong handcuff entirely — and Shipley was himself not practising this week, which is unresolved.

doNotChase.sources: RotoWire · NBC Sports · CBS Sports · Forbes

doNotChase.name: Josh Jacobs
doNotChase.lead: The best player available in either league by season projection, and not available in any sense that matters.

case.label: What the file says
case.body: 84.8% owned, a 167.6 season projection, sitting on waivers. It is the single most attractive-looking line on either wire.

case.label: What it does not say
case.body: He has been on the Commissioner's Exempt List since 31 August. His Week 3 projection is 0.0, which is the file telling you the same thing in the only field that prices availability. This is the runbook's own warning in the other direction: seasonProj is live, but it does not price a player being unable to play.

case.label: And the upside is already yours
case.body: If he were reinstated, Graziano's reporting is that MarShawn Lloyd could keep the lead role — and Lloyd is on your bench. The best case for claiming Jacobs is acquiring a handcuff to a player you already own, with priority you no longer have.

case.label: What would change it
case.body: The NFL reinstating him and Green Bay activating him, both. Until both happen this row stays.

doNotChase.sources: NFL.com · ESPN · FOX Sports · ESPN league file

doNotChase.name: Josh Downs
doNotChase.lead: A 71.2%-owned receiver free in a ten-team league, with a target share that is real — and he still does not get a seat.

case.label: Why the market likes him
case.body: FantasyPros have him leading the Colts at a 27.3% adjusted target share after doubling his Week 1 role, and describe him as the primary chain-mover following Alec Pierce's heel injury. Ownership +6.20 in a day.

case.label: The number that kills it here
case.body: 11.4 projected, against Matthew Golden's 11.4 in the flex he would be competing for. That is a zero-point upgrade for a roster move, and your standing rule declines anything worth under a point.

case.label: The ranking behind it
case.body: He sits at WR37 to Carnell Tate's WR33 and a lower target share. If a receiver is going to take the last seat, it should be the one with the bigger share and the national ownership gap, which is why Tate is a card and Downs is a note.

case.label: What would change it
case.body: Pierce being ruled out for an extended period, which would move Downs from chain-mover to primary and open a real gap over Golden. Or Tate being claimed overnight and Mitchell being taken too, which would make Downs the last man standing rather than the third choice.

cannotSee.label: Whether Chicago has a quarterback
cannotSee.body: This is the decisive unknown of the week and it will not be resolved until Friday at the earliest, possibly Saturday. Ben Johnson said on Wednesday he did not know. Williams is week-to-week with a low-grade hamstring, Bagent is in protocol with no timeline, and concussion protocol is unpredictable by design. Both Loveland cards are built to branch on the answer rather than to guess it.

cannotSee.label: Twelve of fourteen matchup tiles
cannotSee.body: No defence-versus-position table could be retrieved. FantasyPros' points-allowed page and ESPN's matchup-rankings column both render in JavaScript and returned only navigation. The two graded rows — Houston 4th against running backs, Philadelphia 1st against tight ends — came from prose inside start/sit columns, which is a weaker source than a table and is stated as such.

cannotSee.label: Rival claims and tonight's clear
cannotSee.body: ESPN returns only your own pending claims. Waivers clear at 01:00 Mexico City tonight. Whether Carnell Tate, Josh Jacobs or the 49ers D/ST are claimed by someone else overnight is unknowable from here, which is exactly why the Tate card is a branch to check on Thursday morning rather than an instruction for tonight.

cannotSee.label: Saquon Barkley's MRI result
cannotSee.body: It was taken on Monday and no outlet has published the finding. Everything available is pre-result: Rapoport's 'more cautious than anything else', Barkley's own 'I'm alright, we'll know more after an MRI'. He is your RB2 and he carries a QUESTIONABLE flag into a Monday game, so this brief's second-biggest unknown sits in a slot it is not proposing to change.

cannotSee.label: The one-week horizon on the trade
cannotSee.body: The Lamar offer is priced at +3.7 to you and +1.6 to them on this week's projections. Season value points much further in your favour, which is honest to say and is also why LONGSHOT is the right read on their willingness rather than LIKELY.

cannotSee.label: Which drop the app will actually apply
cannotSee.body: In the other league this morning, a card naming one drop resulted in a different player leaving the roster. Until it is clear whether that was execution or platform behaviour, treat every paired add-and-drop in this brief as two separate decisions and confirm the drop on the confirmation screen.
